title: Monday Mode: The Story
premise: A short comedic branching story about surviving a chaotic Monday morning and workday by making small life choices that affect energy, mood, and which ending you reach.
interaction_model: Single-screen branching narrative with tap/click choices, typewriter text presentation, visible health and mood meters, and restart-based replay.
objective: Guide the protagonist through Monday without draining health or mood, and try to reach one of the better endings.
progression: The player moves through a compact node graph of scenes such as waking up, commuting, facing the office, lunch, and afternoon consequences; each choice changes stats and leads toward success, burnout, or alternate lifestyle endings.
theme: Modern workplace chaos, Monday dread, comedy, survival through ordinary adult problems.
mood: Playful, sarcastic, neon-arcade, lighthearted, and slightly chaotic.
likely_audience: Casual players who enjoy humorous interactive stories, quick replayable narrative games, and low-complexity decision-based experiences.
confidence_notes: High confidence that this is primarily a branching choice game because the core content is a hand-authored story node graph with two choices per scene.
High confidence in the workplace Monday premise because titles, story text, endings, and UI labels all directly support it.
Moderate confidence that replaying for endings is the main long-term engagement hook, since the system is compact and built around alternate outcomes rather than deep progression.
recreation_prompt: Create a compact browser-based branching narrative game called 'Monday Mode: The Story' about surviving a chaotic Monday workday. Present it as a single-screen interactive story with a stylish neon-glass arcade UI, a start screen, a visible HUD with Energy and Mood bars, a story card with a large emoji header, typewriter-style text, and two big choice buttons for every scene. The player should guide an overwhelmed office worker from the morning alarm through bathroom decisions, commute moments, office incidents, lunch, and afternoon consequences. Each choice should instantly adjust Energy and Mood, show clear audiovisual feedback, and push the player to the next story node. Include multiple endings ranging from total failure, burnout, and being fired to surviving the day, becoming an office hero, escaping into a lazy day off, or realizing work is not everything. Make the tone funny, slightly chaotic, and relatable rather than dramatic. Add juicy feedback like button particles, success/fail sounds, light screen shake on bad outcomes, celebratory or failure reactions, and a moving abstract background canvas. Keep the loop simple: read a short scenario, choose one of two responses, watch the stats change, and continue until an ending or a stat collapse result appears, then allow instant restart for replay.
